targeted: aggregate factory and coordinate reduction rewrite

findings.evidence: Removed per-allele repeated scans and separately implemented mean/stddev/boolean reducers. Native list adapters invoke the same configured UDAFs as tables. Per-row initializer applies before even an empty list. One borrowed Arrow list slice and one accumulator update per row. Native adapter owns argument arity/type validation; generic collection validation delegates to that contract. Ordered/unordered take now share native table reducer too.
findings.acceptance: Parity across table/list/matrix including large ints, missing calls, haploid/phased calls, empty inputs and row-varying allele count. Complexity O(called alleles + output allele count), independent of allele-count times call-count.

findings.evidence: HailAccumulator::update_batch uses ScalarValue::try_from_array inside the input-element loop for float sum, mean, product and Boolean any/all/fraction; only integer sum, min/max and count_where have native batch paths.
findings.acceptance: Typed Arrow batch kernels or typed loops with no per-element ScalarValue allocation; preserve ordering/numeric overflow, null and nonfinite semantics. Quantify input values processed vs boxed conversions.

findings.evidence: TakeAccumulator::append computes lexsort_to_indices twice in the ordered branch; its first value-only result is discarded when retaining ordered value/key state.
findings.acceptance: One top-k selection per update and retain original value/key pairs; no redundant sorting. Unordered take need not copy whole incoming arrays once n retained.
findings.resolution: One ordered top-k selection retains full value/key state. Unordered take slices incoming values to remaining capacity, compacts the retained output, and ignores later input once full. Lists/matrices now invoke this same native take reducer (including ordered take) with native Int64 n.

findings.evidence: Collection aggregation explicitly rejects nested agg.explode; matrix list aggregation explicitly rejects agg.fold. These are explicit unsupported cases rather than silently inaccurate answers. Ordered take gap was resolved using shared native kernel.
findings.acceptance: Native layout adapters reuse existing aggregate scope/fold semantics, not separate per-domain kernels. Add nested collection/matrix scope coverage.

findings.evidence: Expression-valued one_sided builds if_else over two separate hardy_weinberg_test aggregate expressions. Both aggregate states may count the same calls when mode cannot be selected before planning.
findings.acceptance: Assess actual optimized execution; if both states execute, share genotype count state and apply mode at finalization, with lazy/global/aggregate mode semantics retained.

findings.evidence: Direct entry sum retains its existing Arrow list-sum kernel, mapping absent cells to missing and casting to declared widened result first. This is an efficient layout specialization but remains distinct from HailAccumulator API.
findings.acceptance: Explicit parity for widened int64, float64, empty/all-missing, sparse cells, overflow and nonfinite input; move shared semantics down if any mismatch.

findings.evidence: Collection visitor wraps a mapped IR subtree using declared aggregate result type as a transient frontend placeholder, while native dtype_scoped infers actual mapped input type. Matrix visitor typed() creates a schema-only table projection probe to recover native inferred type. No runtime wrong cast is performed, but frontend type placeholders/probes complicate native-handle architecture.
findings.acceptance: Expose direct scoped native expression type inference with lambda bindings, remove temporary incorrect frontend type wrappers and table projection probes. Check captured globals and lambda context without any execution.
